name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,164

clue.text: Identify Eastern fellow going west

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftward, so the letters run back from right to left

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone tries to pin down a man from the Orient who is travelling westward.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass word for direction is the turnaround signal, read along an across light.
explanation.definitionFit: To name something is to identify it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Cheap ornament in prison can upset folk ultimately

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something turns it upside down, so the letters run bottom to top
ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: nick is British slang for a prison or police station
taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tacky trinket kept in a jail cell somehow annoys people in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is everyday British slang for prison. The spelling NICK-NACK is a variant of knick-knack.
explanation.definitionFit: A knick-knack is a small inexpensive decorative trinket, exactly a cheap ornament.

clue.text: Drink and nuts around start of evening

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so one piece goes outside another
the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: nuts means crazy, mad
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink and a bowl of nuts as the evening begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like a snack beside the drink, but it is the adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an old alcoholic beverage made from fermented honey, an example of a drink.

clue.text: What may be offered by therapist? Service ahead of time

definitions.text: What may be offered by therapist?

blocks.note: Mass is a church service
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A therapist's offer, followed by a note that a service comes before its appointed hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' reads like customer service, but it is the religious one.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage therapist offers rubbing and kneading of muscles as treatment, so the question describes it by example.

clue.text: Elevated space editor secured

blocks.note: a moor is open upland ground
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor has bagged a raised spot, such as a loft or high office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated space' suggests a room upstairs; it is high open country.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is moored has been tied up or anchored, so made fast and secure.

clue.text: One to organise the classroom?

indicators.note: organising things means putting them into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters

explanation.surface: Asking who keeps the classroom in order.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the letters of the phrase rearrange into the person who runs that room.
explanation.definitionFit: A male teacher in charge of a class keeps pupils and lessons in order, so he organises the room.

clue.text: Having two hands operating for a time?

definitions.text: Having two hands operating for a time?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone working with both hands, perhaps a surgeon at an operation
setter's reading: a clock or watch face showing the time with hour and minute hands rather than digits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating' suggests surgery and 'hands' suggest a person; the hands are those of a timepiece and the time is literally the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogue watch displays the hour with moving pointers, unlike a digital display of numerals.

clue.text: Food some require at six

indicators.note: taking only some of the following words means a run of their letters is lifted out

blocks.note: the run straddles the three words

explanation.surface: Some people need their dinner at six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the end of 'require', the whole of 'at' and the start of 'six'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for meals or grub, a colloquial noun for food.

clue.text: Devious spy I get to log as “one specialising in African country”'

indicators.note: something devious takes a twisting, crooked route, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters

explanation.surface: A crafty agent is told to record himself under a cover story as an Africa expert.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase reads like a spy's cover identity; it is the definition, with the country being Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptologist studies ancient Egypt, a nation in north-east Africa, so is a scholar devoted to that land.

clue.text: Hospital transplant? Second thoughts could lead to this

definitions.text: Second thoughts could lead to this

blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: swapping a patient's cardiac organ for a donor's

blocks.clueFragment: Second thoughts could lead to this
blocks.note: second meaning: reconsidering may bring a reversal of one's opinion

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the first reading as a whimsical literal one; the second is the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a reversal of opinion or feeling, which is what reconsidering a decision can produce.

clue.text: Writer’s page introducing Old English

blocks.note: P is the abbreviation for page
OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English

explanation.surface: An author's page begins with some Anglo-Saxon text.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', so the writer is the page put in front of the old language.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author of tales and poems, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Attempt to gain advantage once leader’s left area of influence

indicators.note: when the leader has gone, the front letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a gambit is an opening move made to win an edge, as in chess

explanation.surface: A bid for advantage is made once the boss has quit their sphere of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a political boss; it means the first letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or extent of something's reach, a formal synonym for sphere of authority.

clue.text: Cake and fruit that’s regularly seen in tea party

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a bun is a small sweet cake
a fig is a fruit
the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Cakes and fruit are what you expect to see laid out at a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunfight is a jokey British term for a tea party or crowded social do; the cake and fruit look like part of the scene but are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunfight is informal British slang for a tea party or a busy, crowded gathering with refreshments.

clue.text: Joy crossing lake with daughter and boat crew

indicators.note: to cross something here is to straddle it, so one piece lies across and around another

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a rowing eight is a racing boat crew of eight oarsmen
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Happiness as a rowing crew and a girl cross a lake together.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as daughter plus crew straddling the lake; the crew wraps around it, and the daughter goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight and joy are both nouns for great pleasure or happiness, a direct synonym pair.

clue.text: Clutching mammal, Edward walked uncertainly

indicators.note: to clutch is to grip tightly, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: Ted is a common nickname for Edward
an otter is a river mammal

explanation.surface: Edward staggered along holding some animal in his arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator comes first but belongs to the man's name that follows, which does the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to move unsteadily on one's feet, so the past tense matches walking shakily.

clue.text: Class was first aroused

blocks.note: a class is a kind, sort or type
to be first in a race is to have led

explanation.surface: A school class was the first to be stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' reads as a schoolroom group but means category.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindling a feeling or interest means stirring it into life, so the past tense is a figurative synonym for awakened.

clue.text: Marks runs

blocks.note: first meaning: short horizontal punctuation strokes
second meaning: sprints or hurries

explanation.walkthrough: Both words can be nouns or verbs; the punctuation sense of the first and the verb sense of the second are the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both punctuation strokes on a page and the action of rushing somewhere quickly.

clue.text: Change with time being put back creates alarm

indicators.note: putting something back moves it from its place toward the rear, so it leaves its spot in the word

blocks.note: to change is to alter
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Putting the clocks back when the hour changes causes a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The time letter is lifted out of the verb for change and moved to the end, as clocks are put back in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a warning signal, the same noun sense as an alarm sounding danger.

clue.text: Beast pauses every so often

indicators.note: something done every so often happens at intervals, so only spaced-out letters are kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: An animal stops now and then on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: The even-placed letters of the verb give a stubborn animal famous for halting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a donkey, an example of a beast of burden.

clue.text: Tumbled down hill

blocks.note: first meaning: dropped to the ground, past tense of a verb
second meaning: a mountain or upland moor in northern England

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests rolling down a slope; the slope itself is the second meaning, a northern English word for a hill, as in the Lake District fells.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of a verb for dropping and a regional noun for a mountain.

clue.text: Greek character entertaining any number in Sicilian location

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house, so one piece takes another in

blocks.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
N stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: A Greek man playing host to a crowd somewhere in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on the east coast of Sicily, an example of a place there.

clue.text: Dog gets in shelter, having been disturbed

indicators.note: what is disturbed is knocked out of its proper order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A frightened dog takes cover after being upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The words between the dog and the indicator look like the story but are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The English setter is a long-haired gundog breed, an example of a dog.

clue.text: Literary device TS Eliot transformed

indicators.note: a thing transformed is changed in form, so the letters take a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters

explanation.surface: A poet who changed literature by his techniques.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's name looks like part of the literary picture, but it supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is a figure of speech using understatement by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad', so a rhetorical device.

clue.text: Fat boy eating last of dinner

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece is put within another
the last of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chubby boy finishes off the remains of his dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' reads as an adjective describing the boy, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking, an example of the noun.
